## Introduction

A professional website should be visually appealing, easy to navigate, and consistent across its pages.

While developing my Quarto portfolio, I explored how CSS and SCSS can improve website design, readability, and the overall user experience.

## What Is CSS?

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is a styling language used to control the visual appearance of web pages.

CSS allows developers to customize:

- Colors and backgrounds
- Fonts and typography
- Spacing and alignment
- Navigation menus
- Images and borders
- Responsive layouts

For my portfolio, I created a separate file named `styles.css` to customize the website's appearance.

## How I Applied CSS to My Portfolio

### 1. Creating a Professional Color Palette

I selected navy blue, soft blue, and white to create a professional visual identity.

```css
body {
  background-color: #FAFBFD;
  color: #263449;
  font-family: "Segoe UI", Arial, sans-serif;
}
```

### 2. Designing the Hero Section

I used a gradient background to highlight my name, professional background, and photograph.

```css
.hero-section {
  background: linear-gradient(
    135deg,
    #14253B,
    #355D87
  );
  color: white;
  padding: 65px 45px;
}
```

### 3. Customizing My Professional Photograph

CSS allowed me to adjust the size, shape, and presentation of my profile picture.

```css
.profile-photo {
  width: 220px;
  height: 285px;
  object-fit: cover;
  border-radius: 14px;
  border: 4px solid white;
}
```

### 4. Improving Mobile Responsiveness

Responsive design allows websites to adapt to different screen sizes.

```css
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .hero-section {
    padding: 40px 20px;
  }

  .hero-section .columns {
    flex-direction: column;
  }
}
```

## What Is SCSS?

SCSS (Sassy CSS) is a syntax of Sass, a CSS preprocessor that extends traditional CSS.

SCSS supports features such as variables, nesting, and reusable styling rules.

For example:

```scss
$primary-color: #14253B;
$secondary-color: #355D87;

.navbar {
  background-color: $primary-color;

  a {
    color: white;

    &:hover {
      color: $secondary-color;
    }
  }
}
```

This example demonstrates how SCSS can make styles easier to organize and maintain.

**Note:** My portfolio currently uses a CSS stylesheet. The SCSS example above demonstrates an additional customization technique.

## CSS vs. SCSS

| Feature | CSS | SCSS |
|---|---|---|
| Basic styling | Yes | Yes |
| Variables | Native custom properties | Sass variables |
| Nesting | Supported in modern CSS | Supported |
| Mixins | No native equivalent | Yes |
| Compilation | Used directly by browsers | Compiled into CSS |

## What I Learned

Creating this website helped me understand how Quarto combines content, structure, and styling.

By separating my content into QMD files and my design into a CSS file, I can maintain a consistent visual identity across my professional portfolio.

These techniques are especially valuable in digital marketing because website design influences readability, navigation, user experience, and how visitors interact with online content.
